clue.text: Critical of racialist broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so the letters of racialist are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A commentator condemns a racist programme that went out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like a description of the racialist, but it signals an anagram of RACIALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire mocks and censures its targets, so satirical writing is scornfully censorious.

clue.text: Dismiss ministers as a sign of contrition

parts.note: to dismiss from a job is to sack
the cloth is a collective name for the clergy

explanation.surface: A prime minister sacks the cabinet as a show of remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' suggests government, but here they are ministers of religion, the clergy, known collectively as 'the cloth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitents in the Bible wore rough garments of goat hair to show repentance, hence 'in sackcloth and ashes'.

clue.text: Capital jewellery!

parts.note: capital is read from the Latin for head, so this is jewellery worn on the head rather than splendid jewellery

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising some excellent jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crescent or coronet is ornamental wear placed on top of a woman's head.

clue.text: Neat theft

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so this is the stealing of cattle, not a tidy robbery

explanation.surface: A tidy, skilful robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an archaic word for cattle or oxen, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving off cattle or horses illegally is the stockman's crime of livestock stealing.

clue.text: Running water in road vehicles for making drinks

indicators.note: in places the river inside the word for the road vehicles

parts.note: cars are road vehicles
the Ouse is an English river, and a river is running water

explanation.surface: Water flows through cars to make drinks, as if in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The OUSE is a river in England, a common crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: To carouse is to drink heavily and merrily in company, so someone carousing is boozing.

clue.text: An unemployed baker?

parts.note: a baker makes loaves, and someone idle loafs about, so the jobless one is pictured as a maker of loaves

explanation.surface: A question about a baker who has lost his job.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler who lounges about doing no work is said to loaf, the word punning on bread loaves.

clue.text: A scholar turned and snapped — there are limits

definitions.note: plural definition for a singular noun meaning bounds or scope

indicators.note: turned means the scholar's letters are read backwards

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
snapped as in a dog that snapped, or bit

explanation.surface: An academic lost their temper and lashed out, but there are boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapped' looks like losing one's temper, but it is the past tense of bite; 'turned' reverses the scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means the scope or extent of something, the boundaries within which it lies.

clue.text: Rural cottage providing home for a writer

indicators.note: the two words house the writer's name within them, spanning the word break

explanation.surface: A country cottage gives an author somewhere to live.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across 'ruRAL COTTage'; Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Being a sporting person, tolerate many a lady-killer

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport
to bear is to tolerate
D is 500 in Roman numerals, so many

explanation.surface: A sporty type who puts up with things is a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLUE is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman; 'lady-killer' is taken literally for the fairy-tale murderer of his wives.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk tale the wife-murderer kept the bodies of his former brides in a locked room.

clue.text: It should be included in the charge

indicators.note: included in places the word it inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about an item that ought to be in the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an accusation or a price, but here it is a levy owed to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income paid to support the church is a levy on parishioners.

clue.text: Less well-bred though sound runner

indicators.note: sound tells us a word for runner is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a courser is a swift horse, a runner

explanation.surface: A vulgar person who is nevertheless a healthy athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning healthy, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or unrefined, so one more coarse is more vulgar in manners.

clue.text: Bill's writing article about foreign nobility

definitions.note: read as 'bill is', the possessive standing for a verb

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
c is short for circa, about
a count is a continental nobleman, equivalent to a British earl

explanation.surface: A man named Bill writes a piece about overseas aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is not a man but an invoice; 'writing' is a link. A COUNT is a European nobleman; Britain's equivalent is an earl.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement of money owed to a shop or supplier is an invoice listing charges.

clue.text: Swimmers may move laboriously

definitions.meaning: the front stroke is something swimmers may do
to inch along slowly on hands and knees

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the front-stroke swimming style and slow progress on all fours, like a baby or heavy traffic.

clue.text: A Parisienne going before a board can't be taken in!

parts.note: une is French for a, in the feminine form a Parisian woman would use
a table is a board, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman appears before a panel and cannot be fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going before' is a link. 'taken in' looks like 'deceived', but it means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is inedible cannot be swallowed or consumed.

clue.text: Delinquent demanding a tip in advance

indicators.note: in places the word for a tip inside the word for an advance

parts.note: to make an advance is to offer
a tip is an end, as of a pencil

explanation.surface: A young criminal insists on being given a gratuity up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding' is a link; 'tip' looks like a gratuity but is the end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent is a wrongdoer, someone who breaks the law.

clue.text: Standard weight for a piece of paving

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a stone is a British weight of 14 pounds

explanation.surface: A regulation weight is specified for a paving slab.
explanation.walkthrough: A STONE is an imperial unit of weight (14 lb) still used in Britain for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab of rock laid to form a path or floor is a paver.

clue.text: Storm caused by parking on drive

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the parking letter comes after

parts.note: to drive something in hard is to ram it
P is the abbreviation for parking on signs

explanation.surface: A tempest blows up because someone parked on a driveway.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is to rage or rush about violently, like a rampaging animal.

clue.text: Showing a bit of backbone in game

parts.note: a part is a bit of something
a ridge is a backbone, as the spine of a hill or roof

explanation.surface: Someone shows courage while playing a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backbone' looks like courage, but it is the spine-like crest of a hill; 'game' means birds shot for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump ground bird shot for sport and food is one of Britain's classic game birds.

clue.text: People engaged in trade may well be nameless

indicators.note: suggests that the word nameless could become something else when its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traders are often anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may well be' is the anagram signal on NAMELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who sell goods for a living are commercial representatives or shop sellers.

clue.text: Get through waterfall willy-nilly

parts.note: per is Latin for through, by means of
force is a northern English word for a waterfall, from Old Norse

explanation.surface: Somehow, whether you like it or not, you must pass through the falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link. FORCE is a dialect word for a waterfall in the Lake District and Yorkshire, as in Aira Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce means of necessity, whether one wishes it or not.

clue.text: A principal man needs little publicity

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
an ad is a short advertisement, small publicity

explanation.surface: A leading actor needs only modest promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal man' looks like a lead role, but 'A principal' is the definition, as in a school's headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal of a school or college is its chief, the person in charge.

clue.text: For a creditor to accommodate a number could be a bloomer

indicators.note: the creditor's word takes in the letters given by a number

parts.note: a lender is a creditor
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A lender letting a figure in might make an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder, but it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant purple-flowered shrub is a plant that blossoms each summer.

clue.text: Hikers will get excited, seeing this bird

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Walkers are thrilled to spot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get excited' signals an anagram of HIKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The butcher-bird impales its prey on thorns; it is a predatory songbird.

clue.text: Clever British leader (Conservative)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of British

parts.note: conservatives are on the political right

explanation.surface: A smart Tory leader of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British leader' looks like a prime minister, but it is just the letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright person is quick-witted and intelligent.

clue.text: Release of the underworld boss by order

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
to charge someone is to order them

explanation.surface: A gangster is set free by court order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' looks like a gang leader, but it is DIS, Roman ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let go from custody, hospital or the army is formal discharge, a freeing.

clue.text: Fights for pounds in fees

indicators.note: in puts the letter for pounds inside the word for fees

parts.note: dues are fees, as in membership dues
L stands for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Battles over money in charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal one-on-one combats, as with pistols or swords at dawn.

clue.text: Left in moderate dash

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the word for moderate

parts.note: fair means moderate, middling

explanation.surface: Someone on the left sprints at an average pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dash' looks like a sprint, but it means style or panache.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means stylish verve, a natural talent or panache.

clue.text: Fiddle before noon and at one

parts.note: a.m., ante meridiem, means before noon
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone cheats in the morning while at one with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like a swindle, but it means a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amati family of Cremona made famous violins, so one of theirs is a fine fiddle.

clue.text: Wearing requires re-doing badly

indicators.note: badly done letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something tiring has to be done all over again because it was botched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like 'tiring', but it means wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing away, as water does to rock, is gradual erosion.

clue.text: She hasn't a leg to stand on!

definitions.text: She hasn't a leg to stand on!

parts.words: She hasn't a leg to stand on!
parts.note: the idiom for having no case is taken literally for a woman with a fish's tail instead of legs

explanation.surface: A woman has no valid argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea creature of legend with a woman's upper body and a fish's tail instead of legs.

clue.text: Screen riddle

definitions.meaning: a screen is a mesh for sifting soil or gravel
a riddle is a coarse sifting tray for soil or grain

explanation.definitionFit: Both a screen and a riddle are meshes for straining coarse bits from fine, like a colander.

clue.text: Fruit of Argentine origins

indicators.note: origins hints that the letters of the word Argentine are its raw material, reworked into something new

explanation.surface: A fruit that comes from Argentina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins' signals an anagram of ARGENTINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loose-skinned orange citrus, named after Tangier in Morocco.
